target: - Verify enabled rules, indicator parameter names, required intervals, warmup, execution-bar continuity, and funding coverage before interpreting zero trades or returns. A comparison harness must prepare the union of every candidate's intervals and maximum warmup, or build each candidate separately. Missing data must not masquerade as a strategy with no signals.
content:
- For recursive-indicator parity audits, inspect the actual receiver's input count and closed/forming alignment, not only the acquisition warmup or live minimum. On 2026-10-03, the historical receiver used max(DefaultWarmupBars=200, TechnologyKlineLimit), whereas live's baseline was 150; an audit assuming 149 closed bars mismatched every RG0 ATR/ADX value until recomputed from the actual 199 closed bars. Use the same canonical input window/end/index and unchanged tolerance, preserve failed diagnostics, and distinguish auditing with the original indicator functions from an independent mathematical implementation; fresh snapshots do not prove sequential-cache or live parity.
- Distinguish genuine funding timestamps/rates from settlement-mark completeness. Inspect the original engine's missing-mark policy and report applied fallback counts separately: on 2026-10-03, mark<=0 used the observed funding-minute Close, and an old official response returned an empty mark. Reproduce and label that approximation for original-engine comparisons, without zero funding, synthetic precise marks or silent runtime/source repair. A passed accounting audit does not prove exact exchange settlement prices or all real-cost release gates; preserve missing-mark/source evidence and verify current code before reuse.

- When continuing this user's iterative strategy research after a usage interruption, give a phase summary before starting another experiment: completed versions and full replay counts, passed/failed/pending release gates, failure reasons and evidence limits, portable JSON/report locations, actual process status, and the next concrete research action. Read the latest project checkpoint and recheck the actual goal and process state; stale checkpoint descriptions do not authorize restarting a completed run or resuming a paused goal. Preserve real handles for unfinished work, update the checkpoint when a run or audit actually terminates, and distinguish phase completion from achieving the complete strategy objective. This preamble is scoped to research continuations, not unrelated requests.
